entries.name: A Simple Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis
entries.abstract: In this article, it is proved that the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function must lie on the critical line, known as the Riemann hypothesis.

entries.name: Super Guarding and Dark Rays in Art Galleries
entries.abstract: We explore an Art Gallery variant where each point of a polygon must be seen by k guards, and guards cannot see through other guards. Surprisingly, even covering convex polygons under this variant is not straightforward. For example, covering every point in a triangle k=4 times (a 4-cover) requires 5 guards, and achieving a 10-cover requires 12 guards. Our main result is tight bounds on k-covering a convex polygon of n vertices, for all k and n. The proofs of both upper and lower bounds are nontrivial. We also obtain bounds for simple polygons, leaving tight bounds an open problem.

entries.name: Monodromy factorizations of lines on del Pezzo surfaces
entries.abstract: We give a list of monodromy factorizations in the pure mapping class group $PMod(T_{d+1})$ of a torus with d+1 marked points that represent lines on a del Pezzo surface Y of degree $d\le4$. These factorizations are lifts of a certain fixed monodromy factorization in $PMod(T_d)$ that represents Y. In the case d=1, discussed in more detail, we give an explicit correspondence between such factorizations and the 240 roots of $E_8=K^\perp$, the orthogonal complement in $H_2(Y)$ of the canonical class.

entries.name: Tangent Lie Algebras of Automorphism Groups of Free Algebras
entries.abstract: We study an analogue of the Andreadakis-Johnson filtration for automorphism groups of free algebras and introduce the notion of tangent Lie algebras for certain automorphism groups, defined as subalgebras of the Lie algebra of derivations. We show that, for many classical varieties of algebras, the tangent Lie algebra is contained in the Lie algebra of derivations with constant divergence. We also introduce the concepts of approximately tame and absolutely wild automorphisms of free algebras in arbitrary varieties and employ tangent Lie algebras to investigate their properties. It is shown that nearly all known examples of wild automorphisms of free algebras are absolutely wild -- with the notable exceptions of the Nagata and Anick automorphisms. We show that the Bergman automorphism of free matrix algebras of order two is absolutely wild. Furthermore, we prove that free algebras in any variety of polynilpotent Lie algebras -- except for the abelian and metabelian varieties -- also possess absolutely wild automorphisms.

entries.name: Parity in vector balancing and reverse Littlewood--Offord problems
entries.abstract: We consider the probability that the random signed sum $ξ_1 v_1 + \dotsb + ξ_n v_n$ lies within a given distance $r$ of the origin, where $v_1,\dotsc,v_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ are fixed unit vectors and $ξ_1,\dotsc,ξ_n$ are independently and uniformly distributed on $\{-1,+1\}$. We demonstrate that, for certain values of $r$, the infimum of this probability is sensitive to the parity of $n$. We prove that, for any $d\geq 3$, there is some $\varepsilon = \varepsilon(d) > 0$ such that for any $n \not\equiv d \mod 2$ and unit vectors $v_1,\dotsc,v_n\in \mathbb{R}^d$, there are signs $η_1,\dotsc,η_n \in \{-1,+1\}$ such that $\|\sum_{i=1}^n η_i v_i\| \leq \sqrt{d - \varepsilon}$. In other words, $\mathbb{P}(\| ξ_1 v_1 + \dotsb + ξ_n v_n \| \leq \sqrt{d-\varepsilon}) > 0$. This is in contrast to the case of $n\equiv d \mod 2$, in which this probability can be zero. In the case of $d=2$ and odd $n$, we give a construction demonstrating that $\mathbb{P}(\|ξ_1 v_1 + \dotsb + ξ_n v_n\| \leq 1)$ can decay exponentially as $n$ increases, improving on the previous best-known bound of $O(n^{-3/2})$.

entries.name: A Fujita-type threshold for the semilinear damped wave equation with Hartree-type nonlinearity and initial data from homogeneous Besov spaces
entries.abstract: In this paper, we study the semilinear damped wave equation with Hartree-type nonlinearity $\mathcal{I}_γ(|u|^{p_1})|u|^{p_2}$, where $0<γ<n$, and initial data possessing additional negative regularity in $\dot{B}_{2,\infty}^{-β}$, $0\leqβ<n/2$. We first establish decay estimates for the corresponding linear equation in homogeneous Besov spaces $\dot{B}_{q,r}^s$, allowing low-frequency data in $\dot{B}_{m,\infty}^{-β}$ under the condition $s+β+n(1/m-1/q)>0$. We then prove the existence of a unique global mild solution for sufficiently small initial data in the critical and supercritical range $$ p_1+p_2\geq1+\frac{4+2γ}{n+2β}, $$ under the remaining assumptions on $p_1$ and $p_2$. Furthermore, for initial data satisfying a positive lower bound, we prove the nonexistence of global weak solutions when $$ 2<p_1+p_2<1+\frac{4+2γ}{n+2β}. $$

entries.name: The inducibility of 6-vertex graphs
entries.abstract: The inducibility constant $λ_{F}$ of a graph $F$ is the asymptotically maximum induced density of $F$ in a growing sequence of graphs. This paper systematically investigates the case when $F$ has 6 vertices (and there are 78 cases to consider up to isomorphism and complementation). We show that flag algebras can compute the sharp upper bound on $λ_F$ in 36 cases of which, as far as the authors know, 30 are new results. In each of the solved cases, we also prove results about the structure of large (almost) extremal graphs. In particular, we establish perfect stability in all 32 cases when the extremal construction has no quasirandom parts. We also present conjectures about the value of $λ_{F}$ for 12 further cases (where the upper and lower bounds are very close to each other).

entries.name: Higher-Order Multifractional Stable Motion: Definition and Fundamental Properties
entries.abstract: We introduce the $n$-th order multifractional stable motion ($n$-MFSM), a symmetric $\al$-stable process ($\al\in(1,2]$) whose Hurst parameter is a function $H(t)\in(n-1,n)$, obtained by a Taylor regularization of order $n\ge1$ of the kernel of the linear multifractional stable motion. It contains the $n$-th order fractional stable motion of Kawai as the special case of constant $H$, and, up to explicit deterministic factors, the linear multifractional stable motion ($n=1$) and the moving-average $n$-th order multifractional Brownian motion ($\al=2$). We prove existence, give the harmonizable representation in the Gaussian case, and show that, if $H$ is of class $\mathcal C^n$ near $t_0$, the rescaled $n$-th order increments at $t_0$ converge in finite-dimensional distributions to the $n$-th order increments of the $n$-th order fractional stable motion of index $H(t_0)$. We then study the dependence structure through the codifference. For $s>0$ fixed and $H(t)\to H_+$ with $(H(t)-H_+)\log t\to0$, we obtain the exact power rate of $τ(X(s),X(t))-c_0(s)$ as $t\to\infty$ away from the boundaries of three explicit parameter regimes, where $c_0(s)=\|X(s)\|_\al^\al$ if $\al<2$ and $c_0=0$ if $\al=2$; the constants are explicit and of known sign when $n\ge2$ or $\al=2$, while for $n=1$ and $\al<2$ part of one regime yields only convergence or a modified constant. In particular this codifference does not tend to zero when $n\ge2$. For the $n$-th order increments with constant $H$, whose codifference asymptotics were obtained by Kawai, we give a self-contained proof with the sign of the leading constants and treat the boundary cases of the long-range dependence criterion $H\ge n-1/\al$; for a non-constant Hurst function this criterion is extended only to functions that are eventually constant.

entries.name: Finite quotients of full surface braid groups and complex surfaces of general type: cyclic, dihedral, and extra-special quotients
entries.abstract: Let $\mathsf{B}_2(Σ_g)$ be the full braid group on two strings on a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$. We compute the number of epimorphisms $\varphi \colon \mathsf{B}_2(Σ_g) \to G$, where $G$ is a finite cyclic, dihedral or extra-special group, under the assumption that $\varphi$ does not factor through $π_1(\operatorname{Sym}^2Σ_g)$. We then apply our algebraic results to the geometric problem of constructing smooth surfaces of general type as Galois covers of $\operatorname{Sym}^2Σ_g$ branched along the diagonal. Notably, when the branching order is at least $3$, we obtain surfaces with positive signature, i.e. $c_1^2>2c_2$. In particular, we construct two $3$-dimensional families of minimal surfaces of general type with $p_g(S)=154$, $q(S)=2$ and $K_S^2=1269$, such that members of different families have the same numerical invariants, the same Betti numbers and the same positive signature, but different torsion subgroups in their first integral homology groups.

entries.name: Set-defined graph classes: $χ$-boundedness meets tropical algebra
entries.abstract: We study set-defined graph classes: hereditary classes whose vertices are assigned fixed-length numerical tuples, with adjacency determined solely by equality patterns among coordinates. These classes arise in structural graph theory, communication complexity, logic, and adjacency labeling schemes. We ask when they are $χ$-bounded, that is, when chromatic number is bounded in terms of clique number throughout the class. First, we prove a decomposition theorem: every graph in a set-defined class can be partitioned into a number of parts polynomially bounded in its clique number, each inducing a union of a bounded number of shift-colorable graphs, that is, graphs admitting a homomorphism to a shift graph. Thus bounded unions of shift-colorable graphs form the fundamental obstruction to $χ$-boundedness in set-defined classes. For full set-defined classes, consisting of all graphs realizable by a fixed Boolean rule on equality patterns, we prove a stronger dichotomy: every such class is either polynomially $χ$-bounded or contains the class of $D$-dimensional shift graphs for some $D \geq 2$. Moreover, we provide an algorithm that, given a Boolean-function description of a full set-defined class, decides $χ$-boundedness of the class. It reduces the problem to feasibility of tropical linear programs, and its correctness follows from a duality with winning strategies in mean-payoff games. Conversely, every integer system of tropical inequalities, and hence every mean-payoff game, can be encoded in strongly polynomial time as a set-defined class whose non-$χ$-boundedness is equivalent to feasibility. This provides a graph-theoretic counterpart of tropical feasibility and mean-payoff-game solvability, linking structural graph theory, tropical algebra, and game-theoretic algorithms.

entries.name: Counting Near-Spanning Matchings in Latin Squares and Steiner Triple Systems
entries.abstract: Montgomery proved that for sufficiently large $n$, every Latin square of order $n$ has a partial transversal with $n-1$ cells, and every Steiner triple system of order $n$ has a matching with $\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1$ edges, thus confirming the Ryser-Brualdi-Stein conjecture for even $n$ and the conjecture of Brouwer. We prove sharp enumerative refinements of these results: there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, for sufficiently large $n$, (1) every Latin square of order $n$ has $ \left((1\pm n^{-c})\frac{n}{\mathrm {e}^2}\right)^n$ partial transversals with $n-1$ cells; (2) every Steiner triple system of order $n$ has $ \left((1\pm n^{-c})\frac{n}{2\mathrm {e}^2}\right)^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}$ matchings with $\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1$ edges. The first estimate confirms predictions of Montgomery and Kelly. We also provide sharp estimates for the numbers of partial transversals and matchings of every smaller size.

entries.name: Taut and Dupin Submanifolds (Updated Version)
entries.abstract: This is an updated version of a paper by the author which originally appeared in 1997. The original paper was a survey of the closely related fields of taut and Dupin submanifolds of Euclidean space, and this updated version includes many results in the field that have appeared since the publication of the original version. The emphasis is on stating results in their proper context and noting areas for future research, and relatively few proofs are given. The important class of isoparametric hypersurfaces is surveyed in detail, as is the relationship between the two concepts of taut and Dupin. Also included is a brief introduction to submanifold theory in Lie sphere geometry which is needed to state many known results on Dupin submanifolds accurately. The paper concludes with detailed descriptions of the main known classification results for both Dupin and taut submanifolds.

entries.name: Curvature rank, numerical dimension, and cohomology growth
entries.abstract: Let $L$ be a holomorphic line bundle on a compact complex manifold $X$ of dimension $n$, and let $r$ be the least integer such that the first Bott--Chern class of $L$ is represented by a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form of rank at most $r$ at every point. For any nonzero coherent analytic sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ whose support has dimension $d$, we prove that $h^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes L^p)=O_\varepsilon(p^{r+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every $0\le q\le d$. This is the exponent conjectured by Ma--Marinescu--Zelditch, up to an arbitrarily small loss. In the extreme degrees $q=0$ and $q=d,$ the bound can be taken to be $O(p^{\min\{r,d\}})$. If, moreover, $X$ is in Fujiki's class and $L$ is nef, then $h^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes L^p)=O(p^{\min\{ν(L),\,d-q\}})$, where $ν(L)$ is the numerical dimension of $L$. This answers a question of Demailly for compact Fujiki manifolds. Finally, for arbitrary $X$, any singular Hermitian metric \(h\) on \(L\) with semipositive curvature and analytic singularities, and any holomorphic vector bundle \(E\) on $X$, we have \(h^q(X,E\otimes L^p\otimes\mathcal I(h^{\otimes p}))=O_\varepsilon(p^{\min\{n-q,b+\varepsilon\}})\) for any $0\leq q\leq n$, where \(b\) is the maximum curvature rank outside the pole set of $h$, and $\mathcal I(h^{\otimes p})$ is the multiplier ideal sheaf. When $X$ belongs to Fujiki's class, the exponent is \(\min\{n-q,b\}\).

entries.name: Large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials and trilinear sums over short intervals
entries.abstract: Recently, Matomäki, Pandey, Pliego, Teräväinen and Wang improved the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate of trilinear sums over short intervals of length $x^θ$, which naturally reduces to estimating mean values of products of three Dirichlet polynomials. Based on recent works of Guth and Maynard and Chen, Gupta and Li on new large value estimates for Dirichlet polynomials, they improved the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate for $θ> \frac{3}{5}$. In this paper, we use their method to improve the Baker--Harman--Pintz estimate for every $\frac{1}{2} < θ< 1$. Our result yields improvements on many problems, including the work of Li on primes in short intervals of length $x^{0.52}$.

entries.name: Normal Limits of the Squeezing Function and Strict Pseudoconvexity
entries.abstract: Let $p$ be a boundary point of a bounded pseudoconvex domain in $\mathbb{C}^n$, $n\ge2$, and suppose the squeezing function tends to $1$ along the inward normal at $p$. We show that $p$ is strictly pseudoconvex if the boundary is $C^{2,α}$ near $p$ for some $0<α\le1$, without assuming finite type or convexity. The proof begins under local $C^2$ regularity near $p$. A comparison of Bergman kernels rules out nonconstant holomorphic curve germs through $p$ contained in the boundary. With these curve germs excluded, rescaled normal translations give rise to a holomorphic semigroup. Classifying this semigroup identifies the normalized kernel limit at selected scales and yields the logarithmic growth exponent $n+1$ for the diagonal Bergman kernel along the inward normal. Under the $C^{2,α}$ assumption, Levi degeneracy at $p$ would give a kernel upper bound with exponent strictly below $n+1$. This contradiction proves $p$ is strictly pseudoconvex.

entries.name: Finite speed Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes and their applications in generative modeling
entries.abstract: We study the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac (OU-K) process, where instead of a Brownian motion, a finite-speed Kac process defines the driving process. The OU-K process can be analyzed through a rescaled, time-inhomogeneous Kac process, characterized by a switching rate from the Kac part, and a convergence rate from the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) part. The law of this inhomogeneous Kac process describes the solution of a wave equation, the Euler-Poisson-Darboux (EPD) equation. For Kac switching rates being multiples of the OU convergence rate, we can explicitly derive this EPD solution via the sum of (the derivative of) two Legendre polynomials, restricted between two Dirac points representing the wave fronts. Using the framework of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMP), we describe the conditional velocity fields of the OU-K process via our polynomial-law-formula. This allows us to apply the OU-K process in a generative flow model. Since the OU-K velocity fields prove to be bounded by the finite Kac speed, the usual time truncations of diffusion models become unnecessary. We demonstrate advantages over diffusion and flow matching models in terms of generation sharpness on singular data sets, while achieving competitive results on CIFAR-10 image generation.

entries.name: On Hilbert's tenth problem over quadratic fields
entries.abstract: In 2026, OpenAI proved that Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the field $\mathbb Q$ of rational numbers has a negative solution. In this paper we study Hilbert's Tenth Problem over the quadratic fields $\mathbb Q(\sqrt2),\mathbb Q(\sqrt3),\mathbb Q(\sqrt6)$. Let $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt d)$ with $d\in\{2,3,6\}$. We prove that there is no algorithm to decide for any polynomial equation $P(x_1,\ldots,x_{48})=0$ with integer coefficients whether it has solutions with $x_1,\ldots,x_{48}\in K$. We also show the existence of a polynomial $f(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{25})$ with integer coefficients such that $a\in K$ is a rational integer if and only if $f(a,x_1,\ldots,x_{25})=0$ for some $x_1,\ldots,x_{25}\in K$.

entries.name: Max-Cut on Token Graphs
entries.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with a positive weight assigned to each edge. A cut of $G$ is a partition of its vertices into two sets $X$ and $Y$; the weight of $(X,Y)$ is the sum of the weight of the edges of $G$ with one endpoint in $X$ and the other endpoint in $Y$. The Max-Cut problem asks for the maximum weight, $m(G)$, of a cut of $G$. The $k$-token graph of $G$, is the graph, $F_k(G)$, whose vertices are the $k$-subsets of vertices of $G$, two of them being adjacent when their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. The phase-reconstruction problem for Heisenberg antiferromagnets in physics can be rephrased as a Max-Cut problem on token graphs. Motivated by this, we study the Max-Cut problem on token graphs, mainly when all edges are assigned the same weight. Our main focus is to bound $m(F_k(G))$ in terms of $m(G)$. We prove that $m(F_k(G))\geq\binom{n-2}{k-1}m(G)$, and that this bound is tight up to a multiplicative factor of $1+O(k/n)$; in the case when $k=c \cdot n$ for some constant $0 < c < 1$, we provide an example where this bound is off by a multiplicative constant factor. We also show bounds for $m(F_k(G))$ for various classes of graphs $G$. Finally, we consider the algorithmic complexity of finding $m(F_k(G))$, showing it to be NP-complete for a constant $k$, and giving evidence that, when the weights take finitely many values, it is not NP-hard for $k\geq n^δ$ for any constant $δ>0$.

entries.name: Lyapunov Theory for Output-to-State Stability of Nonlinear Infinite-Dimensional Systems
entries.abstract: For a broad class of nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems with outputs, we show that output-to-state stability (OSS) is equivalent to the existence of a coercive OSS Lyapunov function in implication form. While establishing this equivalence, we prove that OSS is equivalent to uniform global asymptotic stability modulo output, relate these properties to the vanishing output vanishing state property, and highlight new challenges that do not arise in the nonlinear finite-dimensional or linear infinite-dimensional settings. The results are illustrated by a nonlinear reaction-diffusion system with a nonlinear output map.

entries.name: A sharp dimensional threshold for polygonal bubbling in an almost critical problem
entries.abstract: In this paper we study sign-changing solutions for the problem $-Δu=|u|^{2^*-2-\varepsilon}u$ in $\mathcal B$, $u=0$ on $\partial\mathcal B$, where $\mathcal B$ is the unit ball of $\mathbb R^N$, $N\geq3$, $2^*=\frac{2N}{N-2}$ and $\varepsilon>0$ is a small parameter, so that the problem is slightly subcritical. In \cite{BDP}, Bartsch, D'Aprile and Pistoia proved that, in every dimension, there exist two solutions which blow up, as $\varepsilon\to0$, positively at the origin and negatively at two antipodal points; as a by-product of our approach, we prove their conjecture that the corresponding reduced energy has exactly two critical points, both nondegenerate, in every dimension. We consider the natural generalization in which the negative bubbles are located at the vertices of a regular $k$-gon, $k\geq3$, and we show that the picture changes drastically. When $k=3$ there is a sharp dimensional threshold: if $N\geq13$ the reduced energy has exactly two critical points, a nondegenerate saddle point and a nondegenerate local minimum, which generate two distinct solutions, while if $3\leq N\leq12$ no solution of this type exists. When $k\geq4$ no solution of this type exists in any dimension. Moreover, for both families of solutions found for $k=3$ the nodal set stays uniformly away from $\partial\mathcal B$, in contrast with the case of two negative bubbles, where the nodal set of one of the two solutions touches the boundary, and with the Brezis--Nirenberg problem, where the nodal set of the solutions with the same configuration always reaches the boundary.

entries.name: Brane Tilings and Polygons with Two Interior Points
entries.abstract: We fully classify the brane tilings and the 4d N=1 supersymmetric quiver gauge theories corresponding to toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds whose toric diagrams are convex lattice polygons with two interior lattice points. There are 45 such polygons up to GL(2,Z) transformations and lattice translations: 5 triangles, 19 quadrilaterals, 16 pentagons and 5 hexagons. We identify all 323 toric phases corresponding to these toric Calabi-Yau 3-folds. For every toric phase, we present the brane tiling with its quiver and superpotential, the perfect matching matrix and the F- and D-term charge matrices. For each brane tiling, we study the mesonic moduli space of the corresponding abelian 4d N=1 theory through its Hilbert series and plethystic logarithm, and identify its generators and their leading relations. We also identify the mesonic global symmetry for each brane tiling and determine the superconformal U(1)R charges.

entries.name: The $H^{2|2}$-model and the Anderson model with Cauchy potential: similarities and a conjectured relation
entries.abstract: We highlight strange similarities between the Anderson model with Cauchy potential with energy-disorder parameters $(E,λ)$ and the $H^{2|2}$ supersymmetric sigma field with initial non local conductances proportional to $W_{x,y}=λ^2\left \vert \left (-Δ-E+ iλ)\right)_{x,y}^{-1}\right\vert^2$ where $Δ$ is the discrete Laplace operator. More precisely, looking at the Brownian interpolation of both, we show that they follow very similar equations. Motivated by that we investigate the different phases of the $H^{2|2}$-model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with conductances $rW$ for some $r>0$ and show that whatever $r>0$ the $H^{2|2}$-model displays localized and delocalized phases which are coherent with what is expected or proved for the Cauchy potential with energy-disorder parameters $(E,λ)$. Finally, we propose a conjecture that compares key quantities of the two models and would imply existence of delocalized regime for the Anderson model with Cauchy potential in dimension $d\ge 3$.

entries.name: Disjoint Divisors and Splitting Rigidity under Nonnegative Orthogonal Ricci Curvature
entries.abstract: Let $X^n$ be a compact Kähler manifold with nonnegative orthogonal Ricci curvature. We prove that if $X$ admits two nonzero effective divisors with disjoint supports, then its universal cover splits. As applications, we study the MRC fibration of $X$, and show that when the dimension of a general fiber is $n-1$, the universal cover of $X$ splits as a product of a simply connected Riemann surface and a compact rationally connected manifold. When $X$ is rationally connected, it splits off a $\Pj^1$-factor if and only if it contains two disjoint nonzero effective divisors. Together with the results of Zhang and Zhang, these conclusions give a unified description of the universal cover for all possible dimensions of the general MRC fiber. We also establish metric existence criteria for certain projective bundles.

entries.name: On the long-time behaviour and asymptotic geometry of nonlocal aggregation equations with saturating mobility
entries.abstract: We investigate a two-dimensional nonlocal conservation law with a saturating Lipschitz mobility, without assuming concavity of the mobility. For attractive radial potentials, we establish global entropy well-posedness and exact mass confinement. When the interaction potential is quadratic on the active interaction zone of the solution, the nonlocal convolution reduces to an affine drift. This reduction bounds the total path length of the moving barycentre via macroscopic energy dissipation, establishing strong $L^1$ relative compactness of the trajectory through a late-time core-filling approximation that traps the entropic state via $L^1$ contraction, circumventing the imposition of a uniform bounded variation estimate. This compactness, combined with the energy dissipation, forces the entropic trajectory to converge strongly in $L^1(\mathbb{R}^2)$ as $t \to \infty$ to a unique stationary binary state. We characterize the geometry of this limit, proving an equivalence with measure-theoretically star-shaped sets. We demonstrate that the nonlocal dynamics admit non-circular stationary equilibria and do not select a unique saturated disk absent radial symmetry on the initial datum. Finally, for entropic stationary binary states of finite perimeter, we exclude essentially bounded measure-theoretic components of the support complement under strict subharmonicity of the interaction potential, and rule out positively separated support components under uniform convexity.

entries.name: On the interplay between the anisotropy and the regularity of the coefficients in non autonomous problems
entries.abstract: We establish the local Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers of non autonomous integral {functionals} of the form \begin{equation*} \label{functional} {\mathcal{F}(z) =} \int_ΩF(x, Dz)\,dx, \end{equation*} where $Ω$ is a bounded open set of $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \ge 2$ and the energy density $F(x,ξ)$ satisfies general growth conditions with respect to the gradient variable. The main novelty of this work lies in the identification of a suitable condition on the interplay between the regularity of the partial map $x\to {F(x,ξ)}$ and the ratio of the non uniform ellipticity of the problem that is sufficient to obtain the Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers. Our result extends and unifies those previously known from the literature, including the standard $p-$growth case.

entries.name: On Gromov's Volume Growth Theorem
entries.abstract: Let $M^n$, $n\ge3$, be complete and noncompact, with nonnegative Ricci curvature. We derive the estimate \[ Vol (B(p,R))\le \frac{C_n}{c}(1+R)^αR^{n-2} \] from the radial lower bound $Scal(x)\ge c(1+d(p,x))^{-α}$, where $c>0$ and $0<α<2$. The proof extends Ge's heat-covariance argument by retaining the heat occupation of the set where a chosen scalar threshold fails. Varying that threshold with the source time makes all entropy errors integrable and yields the exact exponent $n-2+α$, without a logarithmic loss. We give explicit examples showing that this exponent is optimal and also allow failure of the curvature lower bound on a set of finite volume.

entries.name: On the chromatic splitting conjecture in coheight $1$
entries.abstract: This article confirms predictions made by Hopkins' chromatic splitting conjecture in stable homotopy theory. A consequence of our main theorem is that a certain map of $K(h-1)$-local $\mathbb{E}_\infty$-rings $\mathbb{S}_{K(h-1)}^{B\mathbb{Z}}\to L_{K(h-1)}\mathbb{S}_{K(h)}$ admits a retract, so long as $p-1$ does not divide $h-1$. If $h=2$ and $p$ is odd, we show this map is an isomorphism. We use methods from the theory of $p$-divisible groups and $p$-adic geometry. Along the way we prove an entirely new kind of "two-tower isomorphism," in analogy with Faltings' isomorphism between the Lubin--Tate and Drinfeld towers, which parametrizes $p$-divisible groups over characteristic $p$ perfectoid spaces with fixed generic fiber in terms of negative Banach--Colmez spaces. Using the two-tower isomorphism, we gain control over the continuous cohomology of the Morava stabilizer group $\mathbb{G}_h$ with coefficients in $π_*L_{K(h-1)}E_h$. To study the continuous action of $\mathbb{G}_h$ on $L_{K(h-1)} E_h$, it was necessary to develop the theory of solid Lubin--Tate spectra. Adapting Lurie's constructions, we attach a solid Lubin--Tate spectrum to $p$-divisible groups over a broad class of solid rings in characteristic $p$.

entries.name: Cobham theorem for expansive bases in orders of number fields
entries.abstract: We prove a Cobham theorem for bases $α,β$ in the ring of integers $R$ of a number field $K$ of degree $d\ge 2$, the bases being expansive, that is, of absolute value greater than $1$ at every archimedean place. The two required conditions are $\mathbb Q(α^r,β^s)=K$ and $α^r R\neβ^s R$ for all $r,s\ge 1$. Under these conditions, a function from $R$ to a finite alphabet is automatic in both bases if and only if it is eventually periodic, that is, if it agrees, outside a finite set, with a function periodic for a subgroup of $R$ of rank $d$. Both conditions are necessary: if either fails, some subset of $R$ is automatic in both bases without being eventually periodic. The proof distinguishes bases with different and with equal prime-ideal supports, using recognisability of constant-shape substitutions and comparisons of exact affine symmetries. The result extends to arbitrary orders, to lattices stable under the bases, and to suitable pairs of commuting expansive integer matrices.

entries.name: Recurrent sets and Lyapunov functions: from topological dynamics to weak KAM theory
entries.abstract: The aim of this survey is to clarify the intimate relations between Lyapunov functions and chain recurrent sets. The study of this subject comes from a seminal paper by Conley and has had recent advances by the so-called Weak KAM Theory for homeomorphisms. We provide a survey of the state of the art, presenting recent improvements and connections with the stationary Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Finally, in order to illustrate the distinctions between recurrent sets in a non-trivial case as well as their dependence on a parameter, we discuss a compartmental model from mathematical epidemiology and a fast-slow version of a prey-predator model with Allee effect.

entries.name: Critical Ising and Temperley-Lieb-Jones States: Cone Haag Duality and the Trivial Algebra Object
entries.abstract: We compute the algebra object of two critical Ising states in the operator algebraic framework of fusion category symmetry. The boundary subalgebra is the even part of the Pauli chain, and its DHR category is the toric code. We treat two models. The first is the classical Ising model in two dimensions, through its row transfer matrix. The second is the Ising chain in a transverse field. For the critical transfer matrix state and for the ground state of the critical chain, the algebra object is exactly the tensor unit. In a second part we treat the critical Temperley--Lieb--Jones chains at $δ=2\cos(π/(k+2))$. For every $k\ge2$ the ground state selected by the vacuum block is pure and has trivial algebra object in the Drinfeld centre of the even part. At $k=2$ this recovers the critical Ising chain.

entries.name: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning of Latent Patient Representations from Multi-Institutional EHRs
entries.abstract: Electronic health records (EHRs) contain rich health information for uncovering latent patient representations and clinically meaningful subgroups. Learning from EHR data across institutions is valuable because representations learned at a single site may reflect local data patterns and lack generalizability, yet pooling patient-level records across institutions is often impractical because of privacy constraints and communication costs. We propose a communication-efficient, non-iterative federated spectral method for learning shared latent representation components from multi-institutional EHRs, in which each institution shares aggregate marginal frequencies and a low-rank spectral summary while keeping patient-level records local. A central server aggregates these summaries with the pooled marginal frequencies to recover both the shared low-rank structure and the canonical row-normalization direction required for interpretable representation recovery. We prove row-wise recovery guarantees and error bounds, with a leading federated variance term matching a corresponding lower bound under explicit regularity conditions. Simulations show that our method closely matches pooled analysis in estimating latent representation components, improves as more sites contribute summaries, and outperforms single-site and existing federated benchmarks across a range of data settings. Applied to real-world multi-facility EHR data for stroke patients, the method learns interpretable patient representations that highlight clinically distinct subgroups and could help inform subgroup-specific care.

entries.name: Growth of subsolutions to fully nonlinear equations in halfspaces II
entries.abstract: We establish sharp lower growth estimates for subsolutions of fully nonlinear elliptic equations in half-spaces, allowing source terms that depend explicitly on the solution. The estimates capture both growth at infinity and blow-up at a finite distance from the boundary. Our approach extends the ODE-based method introduced in [J. Differential Equations 320 (2022), 143--173].

entries.name: Non autonomous problems with nearly linear growth and Orlicz-Sobolev coefficients
entries.abstract: We establish the local Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers of non autonomous integral functionals of the form \[ \mathcal{F}(u, Ω) = \int_ΩF(x, Du)\, {\mathrm d}x, \] where $Ω$ is a bounded open set of $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n \ge 2$ and the energy density $F(x,ξ)$ satisfies nearly linear growth conditions with respect to the gradient variable. The main novelty of this work lies in the identification of a suitable quantitative balance between the logarithmic degeneration of the ellipticity and an Orlicz-Sobolev regularity of the partial map $x\to {F(x,ξ)}$ that is sufficient to obtain the Lipschitz regularity of the local minimizers.

entries.name: Data-Adaptive Entropy-Based Moment Reduction for Vlasov-Poisson-Dougherty Dynamics
entries.abstract: We develop a data-adaptive entropy-based moment method for the Vlasov-Poisson-Dougherty system with self-consistent temperature. A positive exponential representation augments the physical moments with data-adapted velocity functions. The collision guarantees are independent of basis construction: for every fixed basis satisfying the stated rank condition, the reduced collision step is uniquely solvable, positive, locally conservative and entropy-dissipative. These guarantees persist under a positive empirical cubature method (ECM), enabling structure-preserving collision hyper-reduction. We construct the basis by proper orthogonal decomposition (POD), fit it with a neural network and post-train it through the reduced dynamics. In two-stream relaxation, sustained heating and drive switching, one fixed post-trained basis with thirteen variables per cell attains space-time distribution errors below 0.25% against same-grid full-order solutions. Post-training lowers this error relative to the neural fit in all three tests and to POD in the two driven tests. With full-grid MUSCL retained, matched drive-switching timings give 1.36-2.89-fold online speedups over the full-order solver using 128-1024 velocity nodes.

entries.name: Representations of spectral systems over finite distributive lattices
entries.abstract: A representation theorem is proved for spectral systems indexed by the lattice of down-sets of a finite poset P. Over an arbitrary associative ring, every excisive, homotopy-exact chain system of differential modules is isomorphic to the chain system of a projective P-graded differential module with a single upper-triangular differential. Consequently, every Cartan-Eilenberg system that is excisive and chain generated, together with its spectral system, admits such a differential model. An example over Z/4 shows that chain generation cannot be dropped. A chain system over Z/8 with short exact rows, whose maps commute only up to homotopy, shows that homotopy-exactness cannot be weakened to distinguished triangles in the derived category. Under finiteness conditions the model is finitely generated. The proof combines a derived horseshoe lemma with induction over the lattice, and yields a short proof and extension of Franzosa's connection matrix theory.

entries.name: Submanifolds, restriction of differential operators and Schouten-Nijenhuis bracket
entries.abstract: In this article, we present new formulas for restricting the Hodge operator, the codifferential and the Hodge Laplacian to a submanifold. These formulas are concise, thanks to the use of tools for differential forms (Schouten-Nijenhuis bracket and generalized interior product). They also facilitate explicit calculations for practical applications.

entries.name: The moments and asymptotic spectral distribution of the Grassmannian ensemble
entries.abstract: In this paper, we study random density matrices constructed by taking partial traces of projections onto random subspaces of a bipartite Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B}$ distributed according to the pushforward measure of the action of the unitary group on the Grassmannian $\text{Gr}_{n}(\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_{B})$. This ensemble models a `typical' quantum subspace. All tracial moments of the density operator, as well as mixed tracial moments of reduced density operators, are computed explicitly using Weingarten calculus. There are several consequences of these results. In particular, we prove that the empirical spectral distribution of the density operator converges almost surely to a rescaled Marchenko-Pastur law. We also prove that this ensemble can be written as a sum of asymptotically free random density operators, leading to an alternative proof of the convergence of the spectral distribution. Finally, we compute the asymptotic expansion of the average entanglement entropy.

entries.name: Large orbits of $p$-groups on conjugacy classes of arbitrary finite groups
entries.abstract: Let $P$ be a $p$-group that acts faithfully and coprimely on a finite group $H$. In a previous paper it was shown that if $H$ is solvable, then there exists a conjugacy class $c$ of $H$ whose stabilizer in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$, and that this bound is best possible. In this paper we remove the hypothesis that $H$ is solvable. As a consequence, there always exists an irreducible character of $H$ whose inertia group in $P$ has order at most $|P|^{1/2}$. The proof depends on the classification of finite simple groups. Its main new ingredient is a result on quasiprimitive linear actions of $p$-nilpotent groups which shows that the elements acting as field automorphisms can be ignored when one looks for vectors with small stabilizers. We also present a new family of examples, with nonsolvable $H$, in which the bound is attained.

entries.name: Sharp Last-Iterate Bounds for the Stochastic subGradient Method
entries.abstract: We determine the worst-case expected optimization error of the last iterate of constant-stepsize projected Stochastic subGradient Method on convex Lipschitz objectives. The upper and lower bounds match up to universal constants for every stepsize, horizon, dimension, and conditional noise moment of order $p\in[1,\infty]$. With bounded noise and a fixed positive bound on the initial distance to a minimizer, the best constant stepsize gives worst-case error after $n$ iterates of order $1/\sqrt n$ on the line and $\sqrt{\log n/(n\log\log n)}$ in every fixed dimension at least two.

entries.name: The Thurston algorithm for general entire maps on the complex plane: Existence and uniqueness
entries.abstract: We prove that a marked topological entire Thurston map $(f,A)$ of stable parabolic type is Thurston equivalent relative to $A$ to a postsingularly finite entire function if and only if it has no Levy cycle relative to $A\cup\{\infty\}$. Here $A$ is a finite forward-invariant set containing the postsingular set. In the realizable case, the entire function is unique up to complex affine conjugacy, and every orbit of the Thurston pullback converges to its fixed point. We establish a Wolff--Denjoy type estimate for nonexpanding self-maps $T$ of the Teichmüller space of any connected orientable surface of finite type without boundary. If $T$ has an unbounded orbit, there are a nonzero measured foliation $G$ and a constant $C$ such that $\operatorname{Ext}_{T^k x}(G)\le C\operatorname{Ext}_x(G)$ for every $x$ and $k\ge0$. For a fixed-point-free transcendental Thurston pullback, this supplies the foliation used in the existence proof. A central tool is a fixed finite measure obtained as the total-variation limit of renormalized pushforward measures transported back along a Teichmüller ray. It allows us to select a cylinder at a late time and compare the mass of the same marked region at different times. If $G$ has a cylinder, a four-point extremal-length estimate and the Thurston matrix force a Levy cycle. Otherwise, in the absence of a Levy cycle, cluster rescaling shows that cylinders of large modulus carry almost all the fixed measure at all late times. Following a cylinder of definite mass until its modulus decreases gives a contradiction. We compare this geometric argument with the proofs for real entire maps and exponential maps.

entries.name: A quasi-tree expansion of the Homfly polynomial
entries.abstract: The Homfly polynomial is one of the best-studied invariants of oriented links. Here, building on work of Jaeger and others, we present a new method of computing it. Terms in the expansion are algebraically simple and they are indexed by certain quasi-trees of the Seifert graph of an (almost) arbitrary link diagram. The quasi-trees, in turn, depend on a single basepoint along the link but no more auxiliary data. This allows us to streamline the proofs of some old results and to find new ones as well, such as an upper bound on the total degree in terms of directed joins of the Seifert graph.

entries.name: Optimal High-Dimensional Martingale CLTs over Rectangles
entries.abstract: We prove Gaussian approximation bounds over rectangles for high-dimensional martingale sums, with lower bounds showing optimality up to powers of $\log n$. The results cover bounded increments, conditional and marginal sub-Gaussian and sub-exponential tails, and uniform $q$th-moment bounds on the largest absolute coordinate for $2<q\le3$. The predictable quadratic variation $Q$ may be random; the comparison Gaussian has deterministic covariance $Σ=\mathbb{E}Q$. We assume $Σ_{jj}=1$ and $\max_j\sum_k|Σ_{jk}|^s\le M$ for fixed $s>0$ and $M\ge1$, allowing $Σ$ to be singular, and quantify the error due to $Q-Σ$. Conditional tail bounds yield the same dimension threshold as boundedness, whereas marginal tail bounds give smaller thresholds. We also establish necessary and sufficient conditions for uniform convergence in all these classes; under the uniform moment assumption, the criterion holds for every fixed $q>2$. When $Q=I_d$, the bounded and marginal light-tail rates have no additional factors in $\log n$ if $\log(ed)\ge\{\log(en)\}^2$; the same holds for the finite-moment rates with $2<q\le3$ in every dimension, for all sufficiently large $n$.

entries.name: A Coats-Based Formulation for Multiphase Reactive Transport Accounting for Aqueous Phase Disappearance
entries.abstract: As part of the energy transition, underground hydrogen (H2) storage in porous media has emerged as an alternative solution for large-scale energy storage to salt caverns. Assessing the feasibility of such systems and ensuring their operation requires accurate modeling of the geochemical processes that may alter the composition of the stored gas. This results in a highly nonlinear coupled system of partial differential equations, ordinary differential equations, and algebraic constraints, calling for robust and specialized numerical strategies. In this work, we adopt a Globally Implicit Approach (GIA), as sequential solution algorithms are known to introduce splitting errors due to the decoupling of flow and geochemical processes. In addition, most splitting-based methods implicitly assume the persistent presence of the liquid phase, an assumption that may be violated during gas injection or withdrawal owing to aqueous phase vaporization and mineral precipitation in the vicinity of wells. We extend Coats' formulation to multiphase reactive transport with a rigorous and fully implicit management of aqueous phase disappearance and reappearance. The proposed approach introduces new molar concentration unknowns for basis species that track the re-appearance of the aqueous phase and guarantee the nonsingularity of the Jacobian matrix. Additionally, the appearance of the liquid phase is managed using a multiphase flash calculation algorithm. The proposed algorithm is validated against the CO2 storage benchmark problems. Finally, the approach is applied to an underground H2 storage in an aquifer under cyclic injection and withdrawal conditions.

entries.name: The Power of Sampling for Finding Far-Apart Bases in Matroids
entries.abstract: We study the geometry of matroids via the \emph{diameter} and \emph{dispersion} of the metric space of their bases. Given a matroid $M$, we ask if the diameter of its basis-exchange graph $\mathcal{G}(M)$ can be approximated by sampling two uniformly random bases. As our main result, we show that their expected distance is always at least $1/16$ of the diameter of $\mathcal{G}(M)$. While this might appear to follow from the edge-expansion properties established by Anari, Liu, Gharan and Vinzant (STOC'19), we show that this inutition is false by constructing a graph $G$ with edge-expansion at least $1$ for which sampling two random vertices does \emph{not} give a constant-factor approximation to its diameter. We turn to finding $k\geq 2$ maximally-diverse bases of a matroid, the $k$ (max--min) diversity problem. When $k=2$, the problem is solvable via matroid intersection. However, for $k\geq 3$ no polynomial-time approximation or hardness is known, even for diverse spanning trees. We show that sampling $k\geq 3$ bases provides a tight $Θ(\log k)$ approximation. We then combine structural insights about the local density of $\mathcal{G}(M)$ with classical LP-rounding techniques to obtain a polynomial-time $1/6$-approximation algorithm for the $k$-diversity problem in arbitrary matroids, the first constant-factor polynomial-time approximation for max--min diversity on any matroid. A key ingredient for our result is the \emph{Farthest Matroid Basis} problem: given a collection of bases, find a new basis as far as possible from all of them. We give a polynomial-time $1/3$-approximation algorithm for this, which is our main algorithmic primitive for $k$ max--min diversity. We also show it is $W[1]$-hard when parameterized by the optimal distance. We also improve the $1/6$-approximation for $k$-diversity, for partition matroids and graphic matroids of constant arboricity.

entries.name: Ehrhard-Type inequalities for radial measures
entries.abstract: We study Ehrhard-type inequalities for convex sets under rotationally invariant probability measures on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge2$, described by a radial density profile $\varphi$. We give sufficient conditions on the profile that apply to Gaussian and multivariate Student measures, including the Cauchy measure, and to a family of mixtures of two Student measures. We also prove necessary conditions on the profile and its tails. Together, these conditions determine the exact parameter range for this mixture family and characterize the rotationally invariant stable measures satisfying the inequality.

entries.name: Star Triangulations
entries.abstract: We study full triangulations of planar point configurations consisting of $n$ points in convex position and one point in the interior, assuming that no three points are collinear (star configurations). Our main contribution is a classification of the star configurations up to combinatorial equivalence. We show that there are $2^{n-1}-n$ equivalence classes, by establishing a bijection between a star configuration and a particular Young diagram. By transforming each such Young diagram to a binary sequence, we manage to also give a combinatorial description of the orbits of these star configurations under the dihedral group action, encoding each such orbit through a black-and-white bracelet. For each star configuration, we derive an explicit formula for the number of its full triangulations, expressed in terms of Catalan numbers and the parts of the associated Young diagram. Additionally we derive a formula of these full triangulations expressed only in terms of Catalan numbers and the bead structure of the associated bracelet. Finally, we let the points move freely under the restriction that they stay in a star configuration and show that there exist $\binom{2n-3}{n-3}$ topologically distinct full triangulations.

entries.name: Intervals of limit points for $B_α$-spectral radii
entries.abstract: For a finite simple graph $G$, let \[ B_α(G)=αA(G)+(1-α)L(G)=(1-α)D(G)+(2α-1)A(G),\qquad 0\leq α\leq 1. \] We study the limit points of the spectral radii of these matrices. Put $a_α=1-α$, $b_α=|2α-1|$, and $w_α=a_α+b_α$. We prove that, for every $α\neq 1/2$ and every integer $d\geq 3$, the interval \[ \left[a_αd+2b_α\sqrt{d-1},\,w_αd\right] \] consists entirely of $B_α$-limit points. All these points are realized by connected bipartite graphs of maximum degree at most $d$. We extend the induced-subgraph interpolation of Alon and Wei from $A$ to $aD+bA$, and obtain a unified proof using bipartite Ramanujan graphs. Consecutive intervals overlap for large $d$; hence the set of $B_α$-limit points contains a half-line for every $α\neq 1/2$. At $α=1/2$, one has $B_{1/2}=D/2$, and the set of spectral radii is discrete. Combining uniform edge subdivisions with generalized Bethe decorations, we improve the Laplacian and signless Laplacian half-line to $[29/5,\infty)$, verified by an exact rational certificate. We also treat two complementary tree constructions. For the starlike trees $T_{1,m,m}$, the limiting $B_α$-spectral radius is the unique solution above the path threshold of an explicit unsquared equation. More generally, letting selected arms of a starlike tree tend to infinity produces ordered limit points with tree realizations. Finally, we give the exact affine relations among $B_α$, the $A_β$-matrix, and the deformed Laplacian. These identify which tree and caterpillar results are reparametrizations of earlier work. The interval theorem also yields half-lines of $A_β$-limit points for every $0\leβ<1$, and of deformed-Laplacian limit points for every nonzero deformation parameter.

entries.name: Well-posedness and finite-time breakdown for Euler-alignment systems with diffusive chemotaxis
entries.abstract: We investigate a recent class of pressureless Euler systems arising in biological contexts, in which the velocity evolution is driven, besides the nonlocal alignment interaction, by the gradient of a concentration self-produced by the population. We first establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, in a class requiring no spatial derivative of the initial population density, together with a continuation criterion. We then derive sufficient conditions on the initial data for finite-time breakdown in the multidimensional setting, with an explicit upper bound for the maximal time of existence. Numerical simulations complement the analysis and illustrate the transition between regular and singular regimes, and the role of the chemotactic strength in the onset of blow-up.

entries.name: Freedom is all you need
entries.abstract: The functional calculus allows for the rigorous analysis of functions of matrices or even operators. The free functional calculus gives the natural class of functions over any category. We initiate the representation theory for taking a generic free functional calculus to the classical nc functional calculus going back to Taylor, Voiculescu and many others, with an eye towards learning of categories. The functional calculus on direct sum closed and locally similarity (i.e. change of coordinates) invariant domains inherits the niceties of complex analysis and large-scale parallel networks, such as automatic analyticity, free universal monodromy, which gives a hypothetical explanation for beneficial overfitting.

entries.name: Minkowski Correlation Functions (MCF): Long-range, robust shape descriptors for point patterns
entries.abstract: A morphometric analysis of point patterns using Minkowski functionals is short-sighted, whereas correlation functions do not provide robust, i.e., additive shape descriptors. To combine the advantages of both standard techniques and to overcome their weaknesses, we introduce ring-based Minkowski correlation functions (MCFs) as robust and sensitive descriptors of disordered point patterns. By assigning to each point a spherical shell and quantifying the resulting two-phase morphology via Minkowski functionals, MCFs capture structural information across multiple length scales, remain sensitive at radii where conventional disk-based Minkowski functionals have saturated, and implicitly encode higher-order correlations beyond the pair correlation and structure factor. We present an exact and efficient algorithm for planar patterns extending the established disk-based morphological approach to long ranges. Applications across scales -- active colloids (Quincke rollers), longleaf pine trees, and the Hubble Ultra Deep Field -- demonstrate clear and systematic deviations from homogeneous Poisson references, with distinct responses of covered area, boundary length, and Euler characteristic. The approach combines short computation times, robustness to noise, and straightforward edge handling with clear interpretability as low-dimensional functions of the outer ring radius.

entries.name: Weighted sum commuting maps with the $(f,g)$-Aluthge transform
entries.abstract: Let $\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ denote the algebra of all $n\times n$ complex matrices, where $n\geq2$, and let $Δ_{f,g}$ be the $(f,g)$-Aluthge transform associated with nonnegative continuous functions $f,g$ on $[0,\infty)$ satisfying $f(t)g(t)=t$ for all $t\geq0$. In this paper, we characterize all surjective maps $Φ:\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C}) \to\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfying\[Φ(Δ_{f,g}(αA+βB))=Δ_{f,g}(αΦ(A)+βΦ(B))\]for all $A,B\in\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$, where $α,β$ are fixed nonzero real numbers. Without assuming additivity or linearity, we prove that when $f$ is nonconstant, $Φ$ must be of the form $Φ(A)=cUAU^*$ or $Φ(A)=cU\overline{A}U^*$ for all $A$, where $U$ is a fixed unitary matrix, $\overline{A}$ denotes the entrywise complex conjugate of $A$, and $c$ is a nonzero complex scalar. Moreover, we completely determine the possible values of $|c|$, which form either $\{1\}$, $q^{\mathbb{Z}}$ for some $q>1$, or $(0,\infty)$. When $f$ is constant, we show that $Φ(A)=S(A)+D$ for all $A$, where $S$ is a surjective $\mathbb{Q}(α,β)$-linear map and $D\in\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfies $(α+β-1)D=0$.

entries.name: Yau's pinching problem and vanishing of Betti numbers
entries.abstract: We prove that a closed connected Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq4$, satisfying $\sec>\frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{n(n+2)}$ at every point has vanishing real cohomology in degrees $1,..., n-1$. It is consequently a rational homology sphere if $n$ is odd or the manifold is orientable. Complex projective space shows that the coefficient is optimal and that the strict inequality is necessary in every even dimension. The required estimate for the Weitzenböck curvature term is established by integrating restricted Ricci operators over orthonormal frames and combining complementary degrees using Hodge duality. This also allows us to replace sectional curvature pinching by intermediate Ricci curvature bounds. For a nonflat metric, the weak Yau inequality, $\sec\geq\frac{\operatorname{Scal}}{n(n+2)}$, gives the same cohomology vanishing unless the manifold is isometric, up to scaling, to a quotient of complex projective space with its Fubini-Study metric. This also holds using the second intermediate Ricci curvature in place of sectional curvature. More generally, a nonzero Betti number in the range controlled by an intermediate Ricci bound forces local symmetry. We also derive sharp Hodge eigenvalue estimates and a scalar spectral vanishing criterion.

entries.name: Differential Transmutations and First-Passage Expansions for Monomial Brownian Boundaries
entries.abstract: Let $P_t=\exp(t\partial_x^2/2)$ be the heat semigroup and let $F(t)=ρt^p$, where $p\ge2$ is an integer. Previous transported-zero theory associates with this boundary a constant-flux solution annihilated by a polynomial-coefficient differential operator of order $2p-1$. We show that the same differential structure contains the complete formal perturbation expansion of the Brownian first-passage density to $F$. For $N=2p-1$ we construct graded spatial operators \[ \mathcal A_r^{(p)}x^n= \frac{(-1)^r}{r!} \frac{\prod_{j=0}^{pr-1}(n+2j+1)} {\prod_{j=1}^{Nr}(n+j)}x^{n+Nr} \] and prove the Laplace conjugacy \[ \mathscr L\mathcal A_r^{(p)}\mathscr L^{-1} =\frac{(-1)^r}{r!}k^r \left(-\frac1k\frac{d}{dk}\right)^{pr}. \] Consequently, the inverse spatial transmutation applied to a reflected Dirac mass generates, coefficient by coefficient, the unique formal solution of the exponential-martingale transform equation for first passage. The cubic case is developed explicitly and checked algebraically through fifth order. We also explain how this differential construction and the independently developed Wright--Volterra generalized-image construction represent the same first-passage law in different coordinates. The present result is formal at all orders; convergence of the resulting perturbation series is left as a separate analytic problem.

entries.name: Recognizing $k$-inducible Digraphs is NP-complete
entries.abstract: A digraph is k-inducible if its arcs correspond to the pairwise majority relation of a preference profile with k voters. By McGarvey's theorem, every asymmetric digraph is k-inducible for some k, but for every fixed k there are digraphs that are not k-inducible. Whether a digraph is 1-inducible or 2-inducible can easily be decided in polynomial time. The complexity of deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible for every fixed $k\geq 3$ has been a long-standing open problem. We prove that deciding whether a tournament is 3-inducible is NP-complete and then leverage this result to show that deciding whether a digraph is k-inducible is NP-complete for every fixed $k\geq 3$. Our results imply that, unless P=NP, k-inducible digraphs cannot be characterized by finitely many forbidden induced subdigraphs.

entries.name: All stable Schoen--Wolfson cones are minimizing
entries.abstract: In the late nineties, R.~Schoen and J.~Wolfson studied the problem of minimizing the area among Lagrangian surfaces in a Riemannian symplectic $4$-manifold. In their parametric approach, they showed that minimizers are smoothly branched-immersed away from a discrete set of points, where there exists a nonflat tangent cone minimizing the area among Lagrangian disk competitors. They also classified the stable singular cones into a family $C_{p,p+1}$ indexed by a positive integer $p$, but left open the question of which of them are globally minimizing. We settle this question by showing that for each $p \geq 1$, $C_{p,p+1} \cap B_1$ minimizes the area among Lagrangian disks spanning its boundary with degree one.

entries.name: A proof of the polygonal Faber--Krahn inequality
entries.abstract: We prove that, for every integer $n\ge3$, the regular $n$-gon uniquely minimizes the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, up to congruence, among simple polygons of prescribed area with at most $n$ sides. We also obtain the optimal linear correction when fewer than $n$ sides are present. The proof combines a partition into convex cells with a mixed boundary comparison. Among convex polygons of fixed area and fixed sum of base angles less than $π$, the isosceles triangle minimizes the first eigenvalue with Dirichlet conditions on the base and Neumann conditions elsewhere. A comparison of Fourier transforms of conformal area densities proves this inequality and the corresponding upper bounds for inverse spectral moments of integer order at least two. We prove strict log-convexity of an interpolation of the eigenvalues of regular polygons of unit area for real parameters at least four. We then derive sharp hexagonal bounds for periodic convex polygonal tilings and asymptotic bounds for convex polygonal partitions of a fixed convex polygon, with an explicit correction for boundary junctions.

entries.name: Convergence of a finite element Chorin projection method for the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations
entries.abstract: We analyze a fully discrete finite element projection method for the stochastic incompressible Navier--Stokes equations with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and multiplicative noise. We show solvability and uniform moment estimates for the intermediate and the corrected velocity approximations under the assumption that the initial data is square-integrable and divergence free, and that the deterministic forcing term is bounded in $L^{q}(0,T;H^{-1}(D))$ for a sufficiently large $q$. Under standard stability and approximation assumptions on the finite element spaces and a coupling condition on the spatial and temporal discretization parameters, we prove convergence of a subsequence to a martingale solution of the stochastic Navier--Stokes equations. The analysis combines the complementary spatial and temporal estimates of the predicted and the corrected velocity approximations and uses the numerical dissipation to identify their common limit. We establish tightness of the piecewise constant temporal interpolations of the velocity field approximations using Aldous' criterion combined with the uniform discrete moment estimates. The convergence result holds in two and three space dimensions as it does not rely on any additional regularity of the limiting martingale solution beyond the one naturally available from the energy inequality. Finally, we demonstrate the performance of the scheme in numerical experiments in two space dimensions for smooth and vortex sheet initial data.

entries.name: Localization of weakly integral objects in braided fusion categories
entries.abstract: An object $X$ of a braided fusion category is called weakly integral if $\mathrm{FPdim}(X)^2$ is an integer. We prove that every nonzero weakly integral object admits a localization, that is, a Yang-Baxter operator $R$ on a finite-dimensional vector space $W$ such that, for every $n$, the algebra homomorphisms from the group algebra of the braid group $B_n$ to $\mathrm{End}(W^{\otimes n})$ and to $\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})$, defined by $R$ and by the braiding, have the same kernel. The operator $R$ can be chosen unitary when the braided fusion category is unitary. This proves the 'if' direction of a conjecture of Rowell and Wang, motivated by topological quantum computation, which states that a simple object admits a localization if and only if it is weakly integral. For a simple weakly integral object of a unitary braided fusion category, the operator $R$ that we construct has an enhancement in the sense of Turaev, and the resulting knot invariant is the Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant of knots colored by $X$.

entries.name: Hölder continuity of meromorphic functions and equisingularity
entries.abstract: For a complex analytic variety and an exponent between zero and one, we study the sheaf of meromorphic functions that are locally Hölder continuous with that exponent for the outer metric. It sits between the structure sheaves of the seminormalization and of the Lipschitz saturation of Pham and Teissier. We prove that these sheaves are coherent and that only finitely many of them are distinct, the exponents at which they change being rational numbers governed by the Rees valuations of the ideal of a certain diagonal. Each exponent defines a Hölder saturation of the variety. We show that a variety whose Hölder saturation is smooth for some exponent larger than one third is itself smooth and that one third is sharp. For reduced curve germs we compute the Hölder saturations from the characteristic exponents of the branches and give explicit thresholds, in terms of classical invariants, at which they become the seminormalization, the Lipschitz saturation, or a curve of the same multiplicity. We prove that homeomorphic curves are bi-Hölder homeomorphic for some positive exponent, whereas bi-Hölder homeomorphisms with exponent close enough to one preserve the multiplicity. We then introduce the relative Hölder saturation of a family and prove that it specializes to the saturations of the fibers over a dense Zariski-open subset of the base. This leads to two notions of equisingularity for families of complex analytic varieties, Hölder equisingularity, defined by a bi-Hölder trivialization, and the stronger Hölder equisaturation, defined by the triviality of the relative saturation. For families of reduced curve germs we show that they interpolate between topological, Whitney and Lipschitz equisingularity, with explicit exponents depending only on the invariants of the special fiber.

entries.name: On the non-uniqueness of solutions of the axi-symmetric swirl-free Navier-Stokes equations, II
entries.abstract: We prove optimal non-uniqueness of Leray solutions of the unforced incompressible Navier-Stokes equations in 3D within the class of axially symmetric swirl-free flows. More precisely, we construct two solutions $u_1,u_2$ that have the same initial data $u_1(0)=u_2(0)$, are smooth for every positive time, satisfy the energy identity, and satisfy \[ u_1,u_2\in C_tH_x^α\cap L_t^2H_x^{α+1}\,\,\text{ for every }\,\,0\leqα<1/2,\qquad u_1,u_2\in L_t^\infty L_x^{3,\infty}\cap L_t^{2,\infty}L_x^\infty. \] Thus non-uniqueness holds in optimal Sobolev spaces and critical Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin weak spaces, even in a symmetry class where smooth solutions are globally regular. The proof relies on a computer-assisted construction of a linearly unstable forward self-similar solution, starting from the numerical profiles identified in our preceding paper (arXiv:2606.07501). We combine explicit asymptotic expansions and global residual estimates with weak coercivity inequalities stabilized by finitely many functionals. Approximate solutions of auxiliary linear equations yield quantitative inverse bounds, allowing us to correct both the stationary profile and its unstable eigenpair by contraction arguments. The instability and localization theorem proved in arXiv:2606.07501 then produces the non-unique solutions.

entries.name: Sharp relations between volume growth, isoperimetry and escape probability in vertex-transitive graphs
entries.abstract: We prove sharp bounds on the probability that the simple random walk on a vertex-transitive graph escapes the ball of radius $r$ before returning to its starting point. In particular, this shows that if the ball of radius $r$ has size slightly greater than quadratic in $r$ then this probability is bounded from below. On the other hand, we show that if the ball of radius $r$ has volume slightly less than cubic in $r$ then this probability decays logarithmically for all larger balls. These results represent a finitary refinement of Varopoulos's theorem that a random walk on a vertex-transitive graph is recurrent if and only if the graph has at most quadratic volume growth. They also imply the existence of a gap at $0$ for escape probabilities: there exists a universal constant $c>0$ such that the random walk on an arbitrary vertex-transitive graph is either recurrent or has a probability of at least $c$ of escaping to infinity. We also prove versions of these results for finite graphs, in particular confirming and strengthening a conjecture of Benjamini and Kozma from 2002. Amongst other things, we also generalise our results to give a sharp finitary version of the characterisation of $p$-parabolic vertex-transitive graphs, prove a number of sharp isoperimetric inequalities for vertex-transitive graphs, and prove a locality result for the escape probability of the random walk on a vertex-transitive graph that can be seen as an analogue of Schramm's locality conjecture for the critical percolation probability.

entries.name: Super Guarding and Dark Rays in Art Galleries
entries.abstract: We explore an Art Gallery variant where each point of a polygon must be seen by k guards, and guards cannot see through other guards. Surprisingly, even covering convex polygons under this variant is not straightforward. For example, covering every point in a triangle k=4 times (a 4-cover) requires 5 guards, and achieving a 10-cover requires 12 guards. Our main result is tight bounds on k-covering a convex polygon of n vertices, for all k and n. The proofs of both upper and lower bounds are nontrivial. We also obtain bounds for simple polygons, leaving tight bounds an open problem.

entries.name: The Kähler-Ricci soliton on bounded pseudoconvex domains
entries.abstract: In this paper, we establish rigidity results for Kähler--Ricci solitons on bounded pseudoconvex domains in $\mathbb C^n$. We first show that if a complete Kähler metric has $C^1$ quasi-bounded geometry and negatively pinched Ricci curvature outside a compact set, then any soliton vector field whose metric dual is closed must vanish. In particular, such a soliton is Kähler--Einstein. We then prove that any Bergman Kähler--Ricci soliton of bounded domains is Kähler--Einstein. Combined with Huang--Xiao's resolution of Cheng's conjecture, this yields a soliton analogue of Cheng's conjecture. We also provide several model domains as examples.

entries.name: The Sample Complexity of Distributed Simple Binary Hypothesis Testing under Information Constraints
entries.abstract: This paper resolves two open problems from a recent paper, arXiv:2403.16981, concerning the sample complexity of distributed simple binary hypothesis testing under information constraints. The first open problem asks whether interaction reduces the sample complexity of distributed simple binary hypothesis testing. In this paper, we show that sequential interaction does not help. The second problem suggests tightening existing sample complexity bounds for communication-constrained simple binary hypothesis testing. We derive optimally tight bounds for this setting and resolve this problem. Our main technical contributions are: (i) a one-shot lower bound on the Bayes error in simple binary hypothesis testing that satisfies a crucial tensorisation property; (ii) a streamlined proof of the formula for the sample complexity of simple binary hypothesis testing without constraints, first established in arXiv:2403.16981; and (iii) a reverse data-processing inequality for Hellinger-$λ$ divergences, generalising the results from arXiv:1812.03031 and arXiv:2206.02765.

entries.name: On min-Storey estimators for multiple testing and conformal novelty detection
entries.abstract: In a multiple testing task, finding an appropriate estimator of the proportion $π_0$ of non-signal in the data to boost power of false discovery rate (FDR) controlling procedures is a long-standing research theme, sometimes referred to as 'adaptive FDR control'. The interest in this theme has been reinforced in the recent years with conformal novelty detection, for which it turns out that similar tools can be used in combination with any 'blackbox' machine learning algorithm. Nevertheless, perhaps surprisingly, finding a solution for 'adaptive FDR control' that is optimal in a broad sense is still an open problem. This paper fills this gap by introducing new $π_0$-estimators, referred to as min-Storey (MS) and interval-min-Storey (IMS), which are built upon the so-called 'Storey estimator'. Plugging these estimators in the adaptive Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure is shown to deliver FDR control both in the independent and conformal settings. In addition, these methods satisfy an optimal power property over any (regular) alternative distribution. The excellent behaviors of the new adaptive procedures are illustrated with numerical experiments both in the independent and conformal models for various distribution structures.

entries.name: The inducibility of 6-vertex graphs
entries.abstract: The inducibility constant $λ_{F}$ of a graph $F$ is the asymptotically maximum induced density of $F$ in a growing sequence of graphs. This paper systematically investigates the case when $F$ has 6 vertices (and there are 78 cases to consider up to isomorphism and complementation). We show that flag algebras can compute the sharp upper bound on $λ_F$ in 36 cases of which, as far as the authors know, 30 are new results. In each of the solved cases, we also prove results about the structure of large (almost) extremal graphs. In particular, we establish perfect stability in all 32 cases when the extremal construction has no quasirandom parts. We also present conjectures about the value of $λ_{F}$ for 12 further cases (where the upper and lower bounds are very close to each other).

entries.name: On some geometrization of compact metric spaces: A solution to the Banach-Ulam conjecture
entries.abstract: We propose a geometrization of compact metric spaces that is based on ideas of S. Banach and J. Mycielski. Then we prove the following conjecture of S. Banach and S. Ulam from 1935: in every compact metric space there exists a finitely additive probability measure, invariant under congruences. Moreover, our techniques allow us to solve a problem of M. Talagrand related to the Marczewski problem and the Banach-Tarski paradox with pieces having the property of Baire. We give also a very simple proof of the conjecture of Ulam about the product Lebesgue measure in the Hilbert cube and explain the existing results about congruence-invariant Borel measures in the language of our geometrization.

entries.name: Double-Scaling Limits for Monitored Haar Products
entries.abstract: We study products of independent Haar matrices interspersed with a fixed corank-one projection. As the matrix dimension $N$ and product length $L$ grow with $L/N\toτ$, we prove that the empirical distribution of squared singular values converges to the free multiplicative Poisson law with $S$-transform $S(z)=\exp(τ/(1+z))$, for both the unitary and orthogonal ensembles. Lagrange inversion yields its moments explicitly, proving Beenakker's conjectured Erlang formula for every moment order.

entries.name: A negative exponent range for Audenaert's complementary McCarthy trace inequality
entries.abstract: Audenaert introduced a class of complementary McCarthy type trace inequalities in his work on completely monotone functions and Bernstein functions; the same problem was later included in the problem list of Audenaert and Kittaneh. The known results cover the corresponding directions for $q\le -2$, $0<q\le 1$, $1\le q\le 2$, and $2\le q\le 3$, while the negative range $-2<q<0$ was left as a conjectural case. We prove the negative exponent inequality, in fact for every $q<0$. After the inversion $X=A^{-1}$, $Y=B^{-1}$, the problem reduces to a trace inequality for the parallel sum $X:Y$. The proof uses the Kubo--Ando mean chain, an Ando--Hiai type log-majorization for matrix geometric means, and a finite-dimensional Schatten Hölder inequality, including the quasi-norm range. We also record that the positive exponent side $q\ge 3$ follows directly from Audenaert's norm-compression inequality for positive semidefinite $2\times2$ block matrices, and in fact holds for all $q\ge 2$. Finally, we determine the equality case on the negative side: equality holds if and only if $A=B$.

entries.name: Counting Near-Spanning Matchings in Latin Squares and Steiner Triple Systems
entries.abstract: Montgomery proved that for sufficiently large $n$, every Latin square of order $n$ has a partial transversal with $n-1$ cells, and every Steiner triple system of order $n$ has a matching with $\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1$ edges, thus confirming the Ryser-Brualdi-Stein conjecture for even $n$ and the conjecture of Brouwer. We prove sharp enumerative refinements of these results: there is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, for sufficiently large $n$, (1) every Latin square of order $n$ has $ \left((1\pm n^{-c})\frac{n}{\mathrm {e}^2}\right)^n$ partial transversals with $n-1$ cells; (2) every Steiner triple system of order $n$ has $ \left((1\pm n^{-c})\frac{n}{2\mathrm {e}^2}\right)^{\lfloor n/3\rfloor}$ matchings with $\lfloor n/3\rfloor-1$ edges. The first estimate confirms predictions of Montgomery and Kelly. We also provide sharp estimates for the numbers of partial transversals and matchings of every smaller size.

entries.name: Curvature rank, numerical dimension, and cohomology growth
entries.abstract: Let $L$ be a holomorphic line bundle on a compact complex manifold $X$ of dimension $n$, and let $r$ be the least integer such that the first Bott--Chern class of $L$ is represented by a smooth closed real $(1,1)$-form of rank at most $r$ at every point. For any nonzero coherent analytic sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $X$ whose support has dimension $d$, we prove that $h^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes L^p)=O_\varepsilon(p^{r+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and every $0\le q\le d$. This is the exponent conjectured by Ma--Marinescu--Zelditch, up to an arbitrarily small loss. In the extreme degrees $q=0$ and $q=d,$ the bound can be taken to be $O(p^{\min\{r,d\}})$. If, moreover, $X$ is in Fujiki's class and $L$ is nef, then $h^q(X,\mathcal F\otimes L^p)=O(p^{\min\{ν(L),\,d-q\}})$, where $ν(L)$ is the numerical dimension of $L$. This answers a question of Demailly for compact Fujiki manifolds.
